@skepagent/skep v0.1.15

Your agents, on every device, in one live session.

Cross-device collaboration for AI coding agents via live join-code sessions.

$ npm install -g @skepagent/skep@0.1.15
Start in 3 steps View on npm

Apache-2.0 · Node.js ≥ 22.12 · macOS & Linux · bin: skep

One master, many peers

Start a session, peers join with a code, and work flows between devices.

/orchestrate 
$ skep session start
join code 7391-4820-1940 · 192.168.1.20:7419
+ macbook, gpu-rig, server joined
> /orchestrate auto
→ split into 3 briefs, dispatched to peers
> /orchestrate confirm
? proposed 3 briefs, waiting for your confirm
> /orchestrate off
→ no auto-split, you route work yourself
✓ summary received · changed files listed

Up in three steps

Run Skep inside any git repository.

  1. 1

    Start a session

    On the master device, open a session. You get a join code and an address.

    skep session start
  2. 2

    Join from another device

    In the peer's TUI, run /join with the code and address. Any repo checkout works.

    /join 7391-4820-1940 192.168.1.20:7419
  3. 3

    Hand out the work

    Let the orchestrator split it (auto, confirm, off, new), or send an intent yourself.

    /orchestrate auto

Also: skep session intent · skep session status · skep ui · skep tui

What's in v0.1.15

Slim join

One line, /join <code> <ip:port>, from any repo checkout.

Orchestrator

/orchestrate auto|confirm|off|new. Default is auto.

Multi-peer picker

Choose which connected peers receive a piece of work.

Split panels

See peers side by side with /layout split.

TUI scroll

Scroll back through output without leaving the terminal UI.

Protocol v2

Output sharing is opt-in, summaries list changed files, and briefs go up to 8000.

Terminal or browser UI

Use skep tui in the terminal or skep ui in a browser.

Session control

skep session start|join|intent|status from the shell or scripts.

D19

Credentials never leave your device

Each device runs its agent with its own login. Provider keys and tokens are never sent over the session, and a peer only shares output if you opt in.
